activities.anchor: Illustration is drawing with a job to do
activities.caption: pair each side of the divide with its line
activities.name: illuJobMatch

config.prompt: Fine art and illustration train differently — pair each piece with its side:

pairs.right: 'make a nine-year-old understand how vaccines train the immune system, in one image, by Thursday'
the way journalists write: fast, legibly, repeatedly, on demand
not photorealism — the trained ability to see form, construct composition, control where the eye travels

config.why: A specific idea, a specific audience, a deadline — that difference shapes the whole training.

activities.anchor: start drawing the shapes and values actually in front of you
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the beginner's biggest jump
activities.name: illuSymbolPredict

config.q: You sit down to draw an eye. What does the trained illustrator draw instead?
choices: The eye symbol, refined until it looks right
The shapes and values actually in front of them
config.why: The shift from symbol to sight is the single biggest jump a beginner makes — and every classical training method, from Nicolaides' schedules to atelier bargue plates, is built to force it.

activities.anchor: A realistic practice loop, the kind foundation programmes prescribe
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the practice loop
activities.name: illuLoopSpot

config.prompt: One line of this practice-loop summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Five two-minute gestures to warm up.
One sustained 30-minute study with measured proportions.
A page of quick object studies — daily if possible.
Skip the variety: one exercise done every day beats all four.
config.correction: The content matters less than the variety: gesture for energy, sustained study for accuracy, negative space for seeing, still-life for values.
config.why: Six months of the loop visibly rewires a portfolio — the loop is the training in miniature.

activities.anchor: is the strongest magnet: the eye
activities.caption: place the midtone share
activities.name: illuValuePlace

config.prompt: A skilled thumbnail's value structure is roughly what share of midtone?
config.why: Roughly two-thirds midtone, one dark accent, one light accent — established before any detail exists, because the eye goes to the sharpest dark-against-light junction first.

activities.anchor: The strongest images pick a decisive moment
activities.caption: drag the divider — peak, or the instant around it
activities.name: illuMomentCompare

config.prompt: Which frame tells the story — drag the divider:

before.label: The peak of the action
before.text: The moment the story resolves — already told, nothing left for the viewer to finish.

after.label: The instant surrounding it
after.text: The decisive moment — where the viewer's imagination completes the story.

config.why: Staging means checking the silhouette: if the key action reads as a black shape, the picture works at any size — the standard thumbnail test.

activities.anchor: A personal style is a consistent set of decisions
activities.caption: file each habit under signature, range or trap
activities.name: illuStyleBuckets

config.prompt: Style, honestly filed — each item goes where it belongs:

items.label: a palette that repeats across your work
a lineweight, and a kind of face
an art director hiring a recognisable way of seeing
the register that shifts between a children's book, an editorial drawing and a game concept
copying a favourite artist's surface quirks before the observational base can support them

config.why: The honest sequence: draw from life until you understand why the artist you admire made their choices, then choose your own — craft first, so style becomes an argument rather than an accident.

activities.anchor: hard edges (a silhouette against the sky) snap attention
activities.caption: direct the eye — choose your edges
activities.name: illuEdgeBranch

config.root: You are directing the viewer's eye across a portrait. Each edge is a decision.

start.text: The craft is the deliberate mixture — where does each edge go?

choices.label: Hard edge at the figure against the sky
choices.feedback: It snaps attention — reserve hardest edges for where you want the viewer to look.

choices.label: Soft edge at the jaw dissolving into shadow
choices.feedback: It recedes — the eye travels on without stopping.

choices.label: Lost edge where two values merge
choices.feedback: The eye travels freely — and an all-lost picture turns foggy.

hard.text: A picture of all hard edges looks cut out; all soft edges look foggy.

soft.text: Soft edges carry the same information quietly, keeping the viewer where the values want them.

lost.text: Lost edges let the eye travel — then the reserved hard edges return it to the emphasis.

config.why: Think in families: group all the darks into one shape, all the midtones into another — the picture reads as three or four big patterns before it reads as objects.

activities.anchor: is where value, edges and composition are rehearsed
activities.caption: line up the workflow, first mark first
activities.name: illuWorkflowOrder

config.prompt: The workflow, tools aside — order it, earliest first:
items: Thumbnail — fist-sized, no detail, flat values only
config.why: At thumbnail scale a bad idea costs thirty seconds and at finish scale it costs two days — working illustrators run four to a dozen thumbnails before committing.
